1. The second respondent lodged the First Information Report on 19.01.2021 alleging that, she is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1 and at the time of marriage, her parents gave dowry in the form of cash, jewelerry, etc.
Accused No.2 is the sister-in-law, accused Nos.3 and 4 are the parents-in-law and accused No.5 is the brother in-law of the second respondent.

The petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 5 along with accused No.1 used to subject the second respondent to cruelty both mentally and physically and also demanded to bring additional money from her Shobha @ Neelambika And Ors vs The State And Anr on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69058609/
2 parental home.

sentences.text: In the month of May 2019, the petitioners-accused and accused No.1 forced the second respondent to leave the matrimonial home, and since then, she is residing at her parental home.
On 15.01.2021, the accused came to her parental home and abused her and her parents in filthy language and also assaulted her.

The police, after investigation, laid the charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498(A), 342, 504, 506 R/w Section 149 of IPC.
3.
The learned Magistrate, after accepting the charge sheet, took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.

Taking exception of the same, this petition is filed by accused Nos.2 to 5.
4.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1- State and the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5.
Perused the charge sheet material.
The second respondent has specifically stated that she was thrown out from the matrimonial home in the month of May 2019.
On 15.01.2021, the petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 5 along with accused No.1 came to the parental home of the second respondent and abused her and her parents in filthy language and also assaulted her.

In the further statement recorded NC: 2023:KHC-K:918 under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., she has stated that the incident on 15.01.2021 has not taken place and the allegation with regard to the incident on 15.01.2021 was made in a fit of anger.

The FIR was lodged after 14 months from the date on which she was thrown out from the matrimonial home, and except omnibus and general allegations, there is no specific allegation made against the petitioners as to how and in what manner they subjected the second respondent to cruelty both mentally and physically and also demanded to bring money from her parental home.

6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582, at para 30 has held as follows:
"30.

entities.text: State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
NC: 2023:KHC-K:918 7.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599, at para 18 has held as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
Shobha @ Neelambika And Ors vs The State And Anr on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69058609/
3 without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

entities.text: Shobha @ Neelambika And Ors vs The State And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.

Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."
8.

In the absence of any material that the petitioners- accused Nos.2 to 5 have subjected the second respondent to cruelty both mentally and physically and also that there was a demand made to bring money from her parental home, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate for the aforesaid offences is without any substance.
Even otherwise, the last of the event has taken place in the month of May 2019 and the FIR was lodged in the month of January 2021 without offering any plausible explanation.
In view of the preceding analysis, the continuation of the criminal proceedings as against the petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 5 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
ii.

The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.457/2021 pending on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC, Shahapur, arising out of Crime No.16/2021 registered by Shahapur Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498(A), 342, 504, 506 R/w Section 149 of IPC insofar as it relates to the petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 5 is hereby quashed.

Sd/-
